description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to restore connectivity and improve infrastructure resilience and road safety in areas affected by Natural Hazards.

The development objective of the Emergency Resilient Reconstruction Project for Ecuador is to restore connectivity and improve infrastructure resilience and road safety in areas affected by natural hazards. The project comprises of two components. The first component, infrastructure recovery and resilience interventions will be assessed against a positive list of eligibility criteria set out in the project operations manual (POM). It consists of following sub-components: (i) infrastructure recovery; (ii) resilience interventions; (iii) activities to complement recovery and resilience interventions; and (iv) acquisition of Ministry of Transportation and Public Works (MTOP's) equipment for emergency response and preventive maintenance. The second component, project management and institutional strengthening for resilience consists of following sub-components: (i) asset management system and planning tools; (ii) capacity building activities, including training, knowledge exchanges, guidelines, and manuals on relevant topics; and (iii) project management support.

title.narrative: Percentage reduction in weighted average travel time in intervened areas

comment.narrative: The end target represents the estimated percentage reduction in weighted average travel time across the eleven road interventions identified for financing under the Project. The calculation considers the expected increase in operating speeds resulting from improved road conditions and, where applicable, reductions in travel distance resulting from restored connectivity along previously disrupted routes. For each road section, travel times are estimated based on assumed operating speeds by vehicle category (motorcycles, passenger cars, buses, and trucks) and the corresponding traffic composition. The final indicator value is calculated by: (i) estimating the aggregated weighted average travel time across the eleven interventions, reflecting the cumulative improvements from better road surface conditions, restored network connectivity, and more efficient travel corridors; and (ii) calculating the percentage reduction relative to the baseline travel time.

title.narrative: Road traffic fatalities per 100 million vehicle-km in intervened areas

comment.narrative: The target reflects the difference between the projected fatalities in the without-project and with-project scenarios for the eleven interventions included in the restructuring. Based on the RSSAT analysis, fatalities are estimated at 74, equivalent to 9.6 fatalities per 100 million vehicle-km, in the base year (2026). By the closing year (2029), fatalities are projected to reach 85 in the without-project scenario, reflecting traffic growth (maintaining 9.6 fatalities per 100 million vehicle-km), and 79 in the with-project scenario (8.84 fatalities per 100 million vehicle-km). This represents a reduction of 6 fatalities, or approximately 7.9 percent in the fatality rate when measured per vehicle-km traveled. The indicator will be monitored using official road crash data reported by the National Traffic Agency and calculated as a rolling three-year average for the intervened corridors.

title.narrative: People with enhanced access to transportation services

comment.narrative: The baseline value remains zero, as benefits will materialize only once the rehabilitation and reconstruction works are completed. The end target reflects the estimated number of people benefiting from the eleven interventions described in the Project Restructuring. Direct beneficiaries are estimated based on an average daily traffic volume (ADT) of 32,125 vehicles (all vehicle types) in 2025. Applying the vehicle occupancy rates used in the economic analysis results in an estimated 68,322 direct beneficiaries. Indirect beneficiaries are estimated at 853,520 people living within a 2-km buffer around each intervention, based on population data from the World Bank geoportal and projected to 2028 using national population growth rates.

title.narrative: Percentage of road safety audits implemented in constructed, rehabilitated, and improved roads

comment.narrative: The project intends to conduct road safety audits on all roads and bridges constructed and rehabilitated under Component 1. Ex-ante road safety evaluations will be carried out by an independent consulting firm contracted under the Project for all eligible interventions. For the Ex-post evaluation, the MIT plans to hire an individual consultant. These audits are mandated by local law, as outlined in the Transport, Traffic, and Road Safety Law of Ecuador, and comply with the Bank's standards. Both the MIT and the Bank team are committed to ensuring the implementation of the audit recommendations upon completion.

title.narrative: Number of women certified for operating heavy machinery

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of local women trained by the contractor in the operation of heavy machinery, as well as in the technical skills required for occupational activities identified in certified road works in Ecuador. The MIT is implementing a training program for women in heavy machinery operation with the objective of building a pool of skilled female operators available for future hiring by contractors. In May 2026, MIT launched the selection process for program participants, aiming to select 100 women. In parallel, the ToR for contracting the training school are being finalized, with the procurement process expected to be launched in June 2026. Each training cycle will last eight months. Additionally, MIT has incorporated gender inclusion criteria into contracts with consultants, contractors, and suppliers, alongside the development of a capacity-building plan and a good practices manual. The Gender Action Plan guiding these activities was approved in August 2025.

This indicator measures the number of local women trained by the contractor in the operation of various types of heavy equipment, such as vehicles, as well as in the skills necessary for occupational activities or other skilled positions identified in road works that are certified in Ecuador.
The MIT plans to conduct a training program for women in heavy machinery operation and road maintenance prior to the start of civil works, with the objective of creating a pool of skilled female operators available for contractors to hire. The first training cohort of 50 women is expected to start in May 2026, followed by a second cohort of an additional 50 women in September 2026. Each training cycle will last eight months. The Gender Action Plan, which guides the implementation of this activity, was approved in August 2026.

title.narrative: Number of MTOP officials trained in the management of road assets and prioritization of road projects

comment.narrative:
This indicator is linked to the implementation of (i) the capital investment plan and (ii) the road asset management system (RAMS). It measures MIT's efforts to strengthen institutional capacity by training its officials and assesses the extent to which they acquire the skills and knowledge necessary to manage road assets and prioritize infrastructure investments effectively. The first training session was held in November 2025, in connection with the presentation of the RAMS ToR prepared with Bank support. 24 MIT officials (16 men and 8 women) participated.
During RAMS implementation, the contractor will develop a comprehensive training plan detailing the objectives, content, delivery methods, number and profiles of officials to be trained, schedule, and the methodology for evaluating training effectiveness. A completion report will be prepared summarizing the number of officials trained, overall effectiveness, and lessons learned. Gender equality will be prioritized.

During RAMS implementation, the contractor will develop a comprehensive training plan detailing the objectives, content, delivery methods, number and profiles of officials to be trained, schedule, and the methodology for evaluating training effectiveness. A completion report will be prepared summarizing the number of officials trained, overall effectiveness, and lessons learned. Gender equality will be prioritized.

title.narrative: Average travel time in intervened areas

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the weighted average travel time across areas where connectivity has been restored or improved.
The current target is an estimate of the potential travel time improvement for five representative interventions in Ecuador identified during project design. Baseline and target values will be revised as part of the Project Restructuring proposed during the Mid-Term Review. It will progressively include sub-indicators for each intervened area, capturing the estimated change in travel time before (baseline) and after the intervention (target).

title.narrative: Percentage of MTOP heavy machinery in working condition

comment.narrative: The MIT is currently analyzing its available machines to categorize them into three groups: (i) those that have reached the end of their useful life and should be scrapped, (ii) those that are in good working condition, and (iii) those that require maintenance to remain operational. Once the universe of machinery needing maintenance has been identified, the MIT will define a plan to (i) determine the necessary maintenance tasks and (ii) execute the maintenance accordingly, depending on the total number of machines assessed and available budget.

title.narrative: Number of road traffic fatalities in intervened areas

comment.narrative:
This indicator will report fatalities after interventions are completed, with an annual average calculated after the second year of implementation.
The baseline is based on applying RSSAT methodology to five potentially eligible interventions. The indicator reflect a rolling annual average of traffic fatalities over the past five years in those areas. Baseline and target values will be revised as part of the Project Restructuring proposed during the Mid-Term Review. It will gradually incorporate sub-indicators for each intervened area and will rely on traffic accident data from the National Traffic Agency (ANT).

title.narrative: Road asset management, including risk monitoring and early alerts system implemented

comment.narrative: The Bank has provided technical assistance to MIT for the development of an asset management system. This indicator will measure whether the asset management system is functional.
